Explainable AI for Practitioners

Machine learning models bahut powerful ho gaye hain — lekin jab model ek decision leta hai, to sawal uthta hai: "kyun?" Explainable AI (XAI) woh field hai jo batati hai ki model ne ye prediction kyun ki, kaunse factors ne use influence kiya, aur model par bharosa kaise karein. Ye SPA usi book ko Hinglish me samjhati hai — sidebar se koi bhi section kholo, beech-beech me 8 interactive labs me haath se try karo, aur ant me Interview FAQs aur Trust Check ke saath apni taiyaari pakki karo.

01Part I · Overview · Chapter 1

An Overview of Explainability

Explainability machine learning ka woh hissa hai jo jawab deta hai — "model ne ye prediction kyun ki?" Pehle ke rule-based AI systems me ye sawal aasan tha, kyunki rules saaf dikhte the. Lekin jab 1980s me neural nets aaye aur phir 2010s me deep learning ne har cheez jeet li, to models itne complex ho gaye ki unke andar kya ho raha hai, ye samajhna mushkil ho gaya. Isi liye explainability ek alag field ban gayi — aur ye chapter usi ki common bhasha banata hai.

Explainability ki kahani — chhota sa itihaas

  • Shuruaat me sab explainable tha: pehle ke AI rule-based chain systems the — prediction kyun hua, ye rules se saaf pata chalta tha.
  • Phir explainability peeche chali gayi: jab neural nets aaye (1980s), to researchers pehle AI winter se bachne ke liye statistical techniques ki taraf mud gaye, jo "explainable" isliye lagte the kyunki woh dusre fields me well-proven the.
  • 2010s me wapasi: jab models bahut achha kaam karne lage lekin koi nahi samajh pa raha tha ki "kaise", to explainability ek alag research field ke roop me wapas aayi — "ye model bahut achha kaam karta hai… lekin kaise?"
  • Aaj ki confusion: bahut si powerful techniques jaldi-jaldi invent hui, aur terms ka matlab har jagah alag ho gaya. Explainability aur interpretability to aksar interchangeably use hote hain, jabki dono ka focus bilkul alag hai.

Explainability vs Interpretability — farak samjho

Book ek real example deti hai: ek knowledgeable industry organization ne authors se ek system ki explainable aur interpretable capabilities describe karne ko kaha — lekin unke definitions baaki industry se ulte the! Yahi confusion is chapter ka maksad hai: aage ke chapters ke liye ek common bhasha aur shared samajh banana.

  • Explainability: techniques jo ek prediction (ya prediction group) ke peeche ka reason batati hain — model ke behaviour ko prediction ke basis par samjhana.
  • Interpretability: model khud kitna samajhne layak hai — uski architecture aur andar ka mechanism kitna transparent hai.
  • Dono alag hain, lekin log inhe aksar ek hi samajh lete hain. Interview me ye farak poochha jata hai.
Yaad rakho: Explainability ka matlab model ko "khula" karna nahi hai — matlab hai prediction ke peeche ka "kyun" samajhna, taaki tum model par bharosa kar sako, usse debug kar sako, aur use behtar bana sako.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — An Overview of Explainability

01.1Part I · Overview · Chapter 1

What Are Explanations?

Jab model ek prediction karta hai, to Explainable AI method ek explanation banata hai — jo batata hai ki model us prediction tak kaise pahuncha. Hum "kyun" dhoondhte hain: kya cheez ne model ko influence kiya, kaise influence kiya, aur model kahan achha ya kharab perform karta hai.

Explanation kya deti hai?

  • "Why did X happen?" — kaunse factors ne prediction ko influence kiya aur kaise.
  • Mental model banta hai: sirf explanation se hum apne dimaag me model ka ek picture banate hain, taaki future predictions ke baare me andaza laga saken.
  • Sirf "kyun" kaafi nahi: aksar hume ek pure explanation se santushti nahi milti — hume counterfactual bhi chahiye hota hai.

Counterfactual — "kyun nahi?"

Counterfactual ek aisi scenario hai jo ulti, plausible wajah batati hai ki X kyun nahi hua. Example: "aaj baarish kyun hui?" ka jawab temperature, pressure aur humidity ho sakta hai. Lekin ye samajhna aasan ho sakta hai ki "baarish isliye nahi hui kyunki aasmaan me baadal hi nahi the" — isse pata chalta hai ki baadal baarish ki explanation ka hissa hain.

  • Counterfactual ko foil bhi kehte hain — original situation ke opposite ek plausible scenario.
  • Ye insaan ko zyada satisfying lagta hai kyunki ye "kya badalne se nateeja badlega" batata hai.

Causal explanation — "X isliye kyunki Y"

Causal explanation aisi hoti hai: "X predict hua kyunki Y tha." Ye attractive hai kyunki isse turant pata chalta hai ki X hatane se prediction Y nahi rahega. Example: "baarish isliye hoti hai kyunki aasmaan me baadal hain."

  • Lekin savdhaan: ye hamesha sach nahi hota — saaf aasmaan me bhi baarish ho sakti hai.
  • Data-focused explanations se causality establish karna bahut mushkil hai (time-series data ke liye bhi), aur koi bhi explainability technique aisi nahi hai jo practically useful ho aur causality ki high guarantee de.
  • Agar tumhe model ya data ke andar causal relationships establish karne hain, to interpretable, causal models ka field dekho — ye book us par focus nahi karti.
Interview tip: "Explainability causality prove nahi karti" — ye ek strong point hai. Attribution batata hai ki kya influence karta hai, lekin ye guarantee nahi deta ki wahi wajah hai.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — An Overview of Explainability

01.2Part I · Overview · Chapter 1

Explainability Consumers — Kaun istemal karta hai?

Ek hi explanation har kisi ke liye nahi hoti. Jo explanation ek data scientist ko chahiye, wohi ek aam user ko nahi chahiye. Book explainability ko teen groups me baant ti hai — inhe samajhna isliye zaroori hai taaki tum sahi technique chun sako.

1. Practitioners — Data Scientists aur ML Engineers

Practitioners explainability ka istemal model banate aur tune karte waqt karte hain. Unka goal: explanation ko actionable steps me badalna.

  • Model behtar banana: architecture badlo, training data badlo, ya dataset ki structure badlo — explanation batati hai kahan problem hai.
  • Accuracy ke alawa bhi chinta: kabhi model data artifacts se influence ho jata hai jo real-world me nahi hote — jaise X-ray diagnosis model me doctor ke pen ke nishaan. Ya model kisi group ke against unfairly biased ho.
  • Data pipeline: kuch features hasil karna mehenga ya compute karna mushkil ho sakta hai. Agar model unhe kabhi use hi nahi karta, to unhe hata do — system behtar hoga.
  • Deploy ke baad: explainability deployed models ki monitoring me bhi kaam aati hai — drift aur skew pakadna, aur batana ki kab retrain karna hai.
  • Aur kabhi-kabhi bas: model ne kuch aisa predict kiya ki tumne kaha — "ye kya tha?"

2. Observers — Business Stakeholders aur Regulators

Observers woh log hain jo model ko design ya engineer nahi karte, aur na hi use deployment me istemal karte hain. Do type hain:

  • Stakeholders (andar ke log): ye non-technical explanation chahte hain — bharosa banana ki model waisa hi behave kar raha hai jaisa design kiya gaya tha. Unke sawaal business-focused hote hain: "kya hume aur training data me invest karna chahiye?" ya "kya ye naya model sahi cheezon par focus kar raha hai, taaki baad me surprise na ho?"
  • Regulators (bahar ke log): ye verify karte hain ki model kuch specific criteria follow karta hai aur aage bhi karega. Ye public organization, industry body, Model Risk Management, ya auditor ho sakte hain. Inki needs technical se lekar vague tak ho sakti hain — jaise ye check karna ki model kisi category (race, gender, socioeconomic status) ke against biased to nahi hai, lekin "fairness" ki koi clear definition nahi di jati. Regulators ko aisi explanations chahiye jo kam human effort me, efficiently aur reliably generate ho saken, kyunki woh model ko baar-baar audit karte hain.

3. End-Users — Domain Experts aur Affected Users

  • Domain experts: inhe environment ki gehri samajh hoti hai, lekin ML ki nahi. Ye explanations ko decision support tool ke roop me istemal karte hain. Example: assembly line par manufacturing defects pakadne wala image model — quality control inspector explanation se dekhta hai ki model ne defect kahan paya, taaki samajh sake ki manufacturing process ka kaunsa hissa kharab hai.
  • Affected users: inhe model ka kaam, data, ya uska matlab — kuch bhi samajh nahi hota. Lekin prediction ka asar in par seedha padta hai. Example: loan offer milne wale log (model ne unki repayment ability predict ki), ya road maintenance ke liye funding paane wali community. Ye bas ye samajhna chahte hain ki prediction fair thi ya nahi, aur sahi information par based thi ya nahi. Aur phir: "mere control me kaunsi cheez badalne se future prediction badlega?" — jaise "kitne time tak on-time loan payments karne se mujhe kam interest rate milega?"
Ek badi limitation: aaj ki zyada tar explainability techniques one-way hain — ML system insaan ko explanation deta hai, lekin insaan ke follow-up sawaal ka jawab nahi de sakta. Ye baatchit nahi, ek requisition form jaisi hai. Chapter 8 me bataya gaya hai ki future me ye kaise badlega.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — An Overview of Explainability
← Prev01.1 · What Are Explanations?→ Next01.3 · Types of Explanations
01.3Part I · Overview · Chapter 1

Types of Explanations

Modern ML solutions complex systems hote hain — data processing, feature engineering, training, serving, monitoring, updating. Isliye explanation sirf model ki nahi, poori pipeline ki ho sakti hai. Aur explanation ka format model ki modality (tabular, image, text) par bhi depend karta hai.

Pre-modeling Explainability — model se pehle, data ko samjho

Explainability ka sabse critical stage model banane se pehle shuru hota hai — sirf data aur features ko samajhna.

  • Model-dependent explanation: "Model ne 90% baarish predict ki kyunki humidity 80% aur cloud cover 100% hai" — ye feature attribution hai.
  • Pre-modeling explanation: "Baarish ki chance ka standard deviation ±18% hai, average 38%" — ye sirf dataset ki property hai, kisi model par depend nahi.
  • EDA (Exploratory Data Analysis): dataset ko summarize aur visualize karne ki techniques — mean, standard deviation, range, missing samples, outliers, feature dimensionality. Tools: Know Your Data, Pandas Profiling, Facets.
  • Multivariate analysis: do ya zyada features ke beech ka relationship — correlation, pair plots, heatmaps, biplots, projection plots (t-SNE, MDS), parallel coordinates. Agar do features highly correlated hain, to feature space simplify karne ka mauka hai — interpretability badhegi. Aur ye interdependencies jaanna doosri explainability techniques ko sahi tareeke se interpret karne ke liye zaroori hai.

Intrinsic vs Post-hoc Explainability

  • Intrinsic: explanation prediction ka hissa hoti hai — model khud explainable hai (jaise linear model, decision tree). Iske liye model me modification ya interpretable model chahiye.
  • Post-hoc: explanation model train hone ke baad banayi jati hai, prediction par based. Is book ki zyada tar techniques post-hoc hain, kyunki ye portable hain aur model se alag ki ja sakti hain.
  • Note: agar koi library prediction ke saath explanation deti hai, to iska matlab ye nahi ki woh intrinsic hai — ho sakta hai service pehle prediction, phir explanation generate karke dono ek saath return karti ho.

Model-Agnostic vs Model-Specific

  • Model-agnostic: technique model ki architecture par depend nahi karti — kisi bhi model, dataset, scenario me use ho sakti hai. Inhe seekhna zyada faydemand hai kyunki reuse zyada hota hai. Ye inputs badal kar, similar predictions correlate karke, ya multiple simulations chala kar kaam karti hain.
  • Model-specific: technique model ke andar ki kisi cheez ka fayda uthati hai — jaise tree-based model me nodes ke weights dekhna, ya CNN me convolution layers.
  • Galatfahmi mat rakho: black-box (opaque) models hamesha model-agnostic techniques use karen, aisa nahi hai — DNNs ke liye bhi model-specific techniques hain. Aur linear regression jaisa transparent model bhi Shapley values (model-agnostic) se explain kiya ja sakta hai.
Yaad rakho: Pre-modeling (EDA) → Intrinsic/Post-hoc → Model-agnostic/Model-specific — ye teen axes hain jinse har technique ko classify kar sakte ho. Interview me technique ka naam sunte hi ye teen sawaal poochho: kab milti hai? kis model par chalti hai? kis scope ki hai?
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — An Overview of Explainability

01.4Part I · Overview · Chapter 1

Local, Cohort, and Global Explanations

Explanation ka scope sabse fundamental farak hai: kya ye ek prediction ke baare me hai, ek group ke baare me, ya poore model ke baare me?

Local Explanation — ek prediction

Local explanation ek single prediction ke liye context deti hai. Example: "is loan application ko isliye reject kiya gaya kyunki credit score kam tha aur income unstable thi."

  • Do similar inputs ki local explanations similar ho sakti hain, lekin ye guarantee nahi hai — technique, model aur dataset par depend karta hai.
  • Ek explanation ko blindly dusre similar input par apply karna safe nahi hai.
  • Example: decision tree me ek node check karta hai ki humidity > 80% hai ya nahi. 80% aur 81% humidity wale do dinon ke predictions aur explanations bilkul alag ho sakte hain.

Global Explanation — poora model

Global explanation poore model ke overall behaviour ke baare me batati hai — saari predictions par.

  • Ye kisi ek prediction ko represent nahi karti — ye model ke behaviour ka survey ya summary statistics hoti hai.
  • Banane ke tareeke: saari predictions (training/validation set) ki explanations generate karke aggregate karna, ya inputs/weights ko wide range me perturb karna.
  • Kiske liye useful: business stakeholders, regulators, aur deployed model ka behaviour original performance se compare karne ke liye.
WARNING — book ki chetavni: Global explanations model ke behaviour ki boundaries batane wale rules nahi hain — ye sirf wahi batati hain jo original training data me observe hua. Deploy hone ke baad, jab model ko naya data milega jo training me nahi tha, to local explanations global explanations se alag ya seedha contradict bhi kar sakti hain.

Cohort Explanation — beech ka rasta

Cohort explanation predictions ke ek subset ke liye hoti hai — local aur global ke beech me.

  • Techniques wahi hain jo global ke liye use hoti hain, bas chhote dataset par apply hoti hain.
  • Sabse powerful use: ek cohort ko dusre cohort se compare karna — isse global behaviour ke baare me aisi insights milti hain jo sirf global explanation se nahi milti.
  • Ye comparison Fairness testing ki buniyaad hai — ek cohort ke liye model kaise perform karta hai vs dusre cohort ke liye, taaki ye ensure ho ki model relevant factors par decide kar raha hai, na ki race jaise irrelevant characteristics par.
  • Example: US historical data par train hua loan approval model — kya usne racial discrimination seekh li hai, ya woh sirf income aur on-time payment history jaise relevant financial background par decide kar raha hai?
  • Note: Explainability aur Fairness ke underpinnings same hain, lekin Fairness ki techniques aur unhe apply karne ka tareeka kaafi alag hai — isliye ye book Fairness cover nahi karti.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — An Overview of Explainability

01.5Part I · Overview · Chapter 1

Attributions, Counterfactual, and Example-based

Explanations alag-alag roop me aati hain — ye depend karta hai ki woh kis type ki information use karke samajh convey karti hain. Teen main forms hain:

1. Attribution-based — "kis cheez ne kitna contribute kiya?"

Sabse common form. Example: "Baarish isliye ho rahi hai kyunki aasmaan me baadal hain" — yahan baadal ek attribute (feature) hai.

  • Feature attribution batata hai ki har feature ne prediction me kitna yogdaan diya.
  • Ye is book ka sabse zyada use hone wala explanation type hai.

2. Counterfactual — "kya hota agar...?"

Counterfactual me proponents aur opponents hote hain. Example: "Baarish isliye ho rahi hai kyunki baadal hain" ko counterfactual me yun kahenge — "Baarish nahi hoti jab sunny hota hai." Yahan "baadal" proponent hai aur "sunny" opponent hai.

  • Humans ko counterfactual explanations aksar pure attribution se zyada satisfying lagti hain.
  • Counterfactual aksar negations me dikhte hain ("baarish nahi hoti jab sunny hota hai"), lekin ye zaroori nahi — "Thand me sunny hone par garmi hoti hai" bhi ek counterfactual hai.
  • Proponents aur opponents dhoondhna modality par depend karta hai: structured dataset me ek negative value opponent samajhna aasan hai, lekin image me ek texture ko opponent samajhna mushkil hai.

3. Example-based (Similarity) — "ye us jaisa hai"

Example-based explanation ek dusri, similar scenario deti hai jo prediction se milti-julti ho. Example: "Baarish isliye ho rahi hai kyunki mausam mostly waisa hai jaisa Rome me baarish ke time hota hai."

  • Similar predictions kyun relevant hain, ye samajhna aasan banane ke liye, ye techniques aksar secondary information bhi deti hain — dataset me similarities/differences, aur model ne dono predictions me kaise behave kiya.
  • Ye "is jaisa pehle bhi hua hai" wali intuition par kaam karti hai — jo non-technical users ke liye bahut natural hai.
Teen forms, ek hi goal: Attribution = "kya influence karta hai", Counterfactual = "kya badalne se nateeja badlega", Example-based = "kis jaisi situation me aisa hota hai". Achhi explainability aksar inme se ek se zyada forms combine karti hai.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — An Overview of Explainability

01.6Part I · Overview · Chapter 1

Feature Attributions — Orchestra Analogy

Feature attribution Explainable AI ka sabse common theme hai. Formally, ek feature attribution batata hai ki ek feature (aur local explanation me uski value) ne prediction par kitna influence dala.

Attribution absolute bhi, relative bhi

  • Absolute: agar predicted temperature 24°C hai, to ek feature ko 8°C ka attribution mil sakta hai, ya -12°C bhi (negative).
  • Relative: attribution ek percentage ho sakta hai — dusre features ke mukable kitna influence hai.
  • Note: Book me "feature influence" aur "feature attribution" aksar interchangeably use hote hain — influence ka matlab hai effect, attribution hai us effect ki measured quantity.

Orchestra analogy — sabse aasan tareeka

Feature attribution samajhne ke liye book ek orchestra ka example deti hai. Orchestra me alag-alag musicians hain — inhe features samjho. Ye orchestra ek competition "ExplainableVision" me hissa le raha hai, jahan ek judge (ML model) har musician ko sun kar predict karta hai ki orchestra kitna achha bajata hai.

  • Har musician ka attribution = usne judge ki rating ko kitna sway kiya, sahi prediction ki taraf ya galat taraf.
  • High attribution: musician judge ko accurate score dene me madad karta hai — ya to woh orchestra ke average talent ke kareeb hai, ya woh bahut time tak bajata hai.
  • Low attribution: musician judge ko galat score dene ki taraf le jata hai — ya to woh bura bajata hai (distract karta hai), ya woh baaki orchestra se out of harmony bajata hai, ya woh itna fantastic hai ki judge poori orchestra ko achha samajh leta hai jabki baaki sab kharab hain.
  • Har case me sawaal ek hi hai: "is musician ne judge ki rating ko kitna influence kiya?"

Techniques ka attribution alag-alag ho sakta hai!

Sahi technique chunna sirf latest ya state-of-the-art method dhoondhne ka mamla nahi hai. Techniques ek hi dataset aur model par bilkul alag, kabhi-kabhi bilkul opposite attribution de sakti hain.

  • Is example me Integrated Gradients (IG), SmoothGrad aur DeepLift ke attributions kaafi close hain, jabki DeepLift conceptually IG aur SmoothGrad se alag approach hai.
  • GradientSHAP apne sibling techniques Sampled SHAP aur Kernel SHAP se strongly diverge karta hai, jabki teeno same underlying theory use karte hain.
  • Feature Ablation kisi aur method jaisi nahi hai, lekin kabhi-kabhi uske attributions dusri techniques se milte hain (jaise RM aur PTRATIO ke liye), aur B aur TAX ko usne aisa influence diya jo kisi aur method ne nahi diya.
  • Sabak: ek hi technique par bharosa mat karo — multiple techniques se cross-check karo, aur attribution ki modality (tabular me numbers, image me pixels, text me tokens) samjho.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — An Overview of Explainability

01.7Part I · Overview · Chapter 1

Shapley Values — Game Theory se Attribution

Feature attribution nikalne ka ek sabse commonly used method hai Shapley values — jo game theory se aata hai. Lloyd Shapley ne ye technique 1951 me publish ki thi, aur iske liye unhe 2012 me Economics ka Nobel Prize mila.

Shapley values ka core idea

Shapley values feature permutation jaisi techniques se alag hain. Permutation feature values badal kar impact estimate karta hai. Shapley values purely observational hain — ye features ke alag-alag groups (coalitions) ke saath predictions test karke attribution infer karte hain.

  • Coalitions: features ko multiple overlapping subsets me group karo. Har coalition ke liye sirf uske features se prediction banao, aur compare karo ek aisi coalition se jisme ek feature zyada hai.
  • Paths: ise dynamic programming problem ki tarah bhi dekh sakte ho — ek series of steps, jahan har step me ek aur feature add hoti hai. Alag-alag permutations ke liye bahut saare paths bante hain.

Worked example — baarish predict karna

Weather dataset: temperature aur cloud_cover se baarish (inches me) predict karni hai. Prediction function P() hai.

  • P({}) = 0 (koi feature nahi — null baseline)
  • P(temperature) = 2 inches
  • P(cloud_cover) = 5 inches
  • P({temperature, cloud_cover}) = 6 inches

Temperature ka Shapley value: P({temperature, cloud_cover}) − P({cloud_cover}) = 6 − 5 = 1. Aur P({temperature}) − P({}) = 2 − 0 = 2. Dono ka average = 1.5.

Cloud_cover ka Shapley value: (6 − 2) aur (5 − 0) ka average = 4.5.

Efficiency property: Shapley values ka sum poori prediction ke barabar hota hai — 1.5 + 4.5 = 6. Ye Shapley values ki sabse useful property hai: attribution poori prediction ko explain karta hai, kuch bhi "bacha" nahi rehta.

Teen features — paths badh jate hain

Humidity add karne par 6 paths bante hain (3! = 6 permutations). Har path me har feature ka intermediate attribution nikala jata hai — prediction ka difference, step se pehle aur baad me. Final attribution = saare paths par us feature ke intermediate attributions ka average.

  • Example: P({}) = 3, P(temperature) = 2, P(cloud_cover) = 4, P(humidity) = 5, P({temperature, cloud_cover}) = 6, P({temperature, humidity}) = 8, P({cloud_cover, humidity}) = 10, P({cloud_cover, temperature, humidity}) = 15.
  • Path 1 me humidity ka intermediate attribution = 15 − 6 = 9. Baaki paths me bhi aise hi nikal kar average liya jata hai.
  • Ordering matter nahi karta: paths me features ka order irrelevant hai — ye Shapley values ki ek important aur sabse zyada galat samjhi jaane wali property hai (causality se confuse mat karo).

Classification models me Shapley values?

Classification models me bhi Shapley values bilkul theek hain. Modern classification models classes ko labels ki jagah vector form me represent karte hain (embeddings ya one-hot encoding).

  • Shapley value ko "ek class ki taraf dhakelna" mat samjho — ye us class ke predicted score ko strengthen ya weaken karta hai.
  • Multi-class ke liye typical tareeka: har class ke liye alag se Shapley values calculate karo, sirf predicted class ke liye nahi.

Sampled Shapley — practical tareeka

Poori Shapley calculation computationally infeasible hai — 10 features ke liye 210 = 1,024 combinations (1,023 additional predictions) chahiye. Isliye practically har Shapley-based technique sampled Shapley use karti hai.

  • Tareeke: kuch steps skip karna, random coalitions sample karke Monte Carlo se average karna, ya gradients follow karna.
  • Tradeoff: ab ye approximation hai — true attribution ka approximate value, with approximation error. Is wajah se Shapley values ka sum predicted result ke barabar nahi bhi ho sakta.
  • Tuning: sampled paths ki sankhya badhao → error kam, runtime zyada. Kam karo → error zyada, runtime kam. Best tradeoff ke liye tune karo.

Shapley values kaise calculate karein — asli mushkil

Shapley values ko originally jaise define kiya gaya tha (features ko poori tarah hata kar observe karna), waisa ML me rarely feasible hai — historical datasets ko "rerun" nahi kar sakte. Isliye alag techniques invent hui hain jo removed features ko handle karti hain — aksar unke liye ek synthetic value bana kar, taaki model ko as-is use kar saken. Example: open source SHAP library ke paas model architecture ke hisaab se chaar alag implementations hain.

  • Strength: decades se use me, academically well-studied, sabse proven techniques me se ek.
  • Weakness: true Shapley computationally infeasible; game theory concepts stakeholders ko samjhana mushkil (trust building me dikkat).
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — An Overview of Explainability
← Prev01.6 · Feature Attributions — Orchestra Analogy→ Next01.8 · Baselines — "Kuch nahi" ka matlab kya hai?
01.8Part I · Overview · Chapter 1

Baselines — "Kuch nahi" ka matlab kya hai?

Shapley paths me hum baar-baar "partial" predictions ki baat karte hain — jaise P({cloud_cover, humidity}) jab model temperature bhi leta hai. Ye partial predictions kaise compute karein? Iska jawab hai baselines.

Baseline kya hai?

Baseline ek aisi neutral ya uninformative value hai jo prediction ko influence nahi karti, isliye Shapley value me contribute nahi karti. Hum in values ko placeholder ki tarah use karte hain jab coalition ke liye partial prediction nikalte hain.

  • Example: P({cloud_cover = 0.8, humidity = 0.9}) = 10 ko asal me aise feed kiya jata hai — P({cloud_cover = 0.8, humidity = 0.9, temperature = 22}) = 10, jahan temperature = 22°C baseline value hai.
  • Baselines vary kar sakti hain — koi baseline kuch predictions ke liye best ho sakti hai, ya ek carefully crafted baseline poori training dataset ke liye uninformative ho sakti hai.
  • Best baseline kaise banayein, ye Chapters 3–6 me discuss hota hai (har modality ke liye alag).

Shapley calculate karne ke alag tareeke

Removed features ko handle karne ke liye kai approaches hain — Conditional Expectations, RBShap, aur doosre. Sundararajan aur Najmi ka paper "The Many Shapley Values for Model Explanation" in approaches ka excellent breakdown deta hai, tradeoffs aur real-world examples ke saath.

  • Core idea: removed feature ke liye ek synthetic value banao jo model ko as-is use karne de, minimal contribution ke saath — model architecture ya final predicted value ko change kiye bina.
  • Assumption: intermediate path steps me features ka order matter nahi karta.
Yaad rakho: Baseline ka chunav explanation ko poori tarah badal sakta hai. Galat baseline = galat attribution. Isliye baseline ko "koi bhi value" mat samjho — ye technique ka sabse sensitive hissa hai, aur Chapter 2 me images ke liye iski gehrai se charcha hai.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — An Overview of Explainability
← Prev01.7 · Shapley Values — Game Theory se Attribution→ Next01.9 · Gradient-based Techniques
01.9Part I · Overview · Chapter 1

Gradient-based Techniques

Gradient-based approaches explainability ki sabse powerful aur commonly used techniques me se hain. Deep learning models by construction differentiable hote hain, aur function ka derivative uske local behaviour ke baare me important information deta hai.

Gradient kya batata hai?

Derivative batata hai ki ek variable me function kitni tezi se badalta hai. Gradient uska high-dimensional version hai — ek vector jo steepest ascent ki direction batata hai.

  • Gradient descent parameters ke space me gradient use karke loss minimize karta hai.
  • Waise hi, inputs ke respect me model function ka gradient batata hai ki inputs badalne par prediction kaise badlega — aur yehi explainability ke liye chahiye: "agar input itna is tareeke se badla, to prediction bhi badlega."
  • Is book ki bahut si techniques isi par based hain — prediction ka value features ke badalne par kaise badalta hai, ye measure karna.

Feature space me path kya hota hai?

Images ke liye: 32×32 pixels, 3 RGB channels wali image ek 3,072-dimensional space me ek vector hai. Us vector ke elements badalna = picture badalna.

  • Gradient-based technique ek baseline image se shuru karti hai aur input image tak feature space me ek path banati hai.
  • Path par chalte hue, har step par gradients evaluate kiye jate hain, aur unse har pixel ke liye attribution value calculate hoti hai — kabhi-kabhi attributions ko regions me segment bhi kiya jata hai.
  • Images ke liye ye technique bahut natural hai kyunki image uniform features ka array hai, fixed linear scale ke saath (0.0 se 1.0 ya 0 se 255).
  • Tabular (Chapter 3) aur text (Chapter 5) models ke liye bhi gradient techniques use hoti hain, lekin baseline ka type alag hota hai.

Shapley values se connection

Agar ye technique Shapley values jaisi lagti hai, to wahi hai! Dono hi individual features ka influence measure karti hain, ye dekh kar ki input me nayi information aane par prediction kaise badalta hai.

  • Shapley: combinatorially — features ko ek-ek karke ya coalitions me add karke, baseline prediction se compare karke.
  • Integrated Gradients: path ke along gradients accumulate karke.
  • Farak: images me features (pixels) ko poori tarah "hatana" rarely sense banata hai — pixel ki location aur neighbours ke relative value bhi important hain (jaise edge detection). Isliye regions ko drop karke influence samajhne ka approach abhi explore nahi hua hai, aur shayad future me interpretable models me zyada use hoga.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — An Overview of Explainability
← Prev01.8 · Baselines — "Kuch nahi" ka matlab kya hai?→ Next01.10 · Saliency Maps and Feature Attributions
01.10Part I · Overview · Chapter 1

Saliency Maps and Feature Attributions

Saliency maps ka matlab hai — image ke kaunse regions ya pixels baaki se zyada important hain. Ye concept computer vision se aaya hai, lekin explainability me iska matlab hai: model apna dhyaan kahan lagata hai?

Saliency maps kahan se aaye?

Originally saliency maps human attention ko samajhne ke liye use hote the — insaan pehle kahan dekhta hai, ye track karna (eye movements aur fixation areas). MIT/Tuebingen Saliency dataset eye movement tasks ka benchmark hai.

Explainability me saliency maps

Explainability me saliency methods wahi kaam karti hain — woh regions ya pixels emphasize karna jahan trained model apna attention lagata hai, prediction tak pahunchne ke liye.

  • Chapter 2 (Image Data) me dekhenge ki integrated gradients se ek mask ya overlay kaise banaya jata hai, jo sabse zyada contribute karne wale pixels highlight karta hai.
  • Gradient-based techniques se aise attribution masks ke saath-saath aur bhi saliency-based techniques milti hain jo image models par apply hoti hain.
  • Saliency map = sensitivity map = pixel attribution map — ye teeno terms aksar ek hi cheez ke liye use hote hain: kaunse pixels prediction ke liye sabse important the.
Yaad rakho: Saliency map sirf "kahan" batata hai, "kyun" nahi. Ye batata hai ki model ne kahan dekha, lekin ye nahi batata ki us region me kya dekh kar usne decide kiya. Isliye saliency maps ko hamesha doosri techniques ke saath cross-check karo.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — An Overview of Explainability
← Prev01.9 · Gradient-based Techniques→ Next01.11 · Surrogate Models — Model ka "duplicate" bana kar samjho
01.11Part I · Overview · Chapter 1

Surrogate Models — Model ka "duplicate" bana kar samjho

Model ke behaviour ko samajhne ka ek aur tareeka hai — surrogate model use karna. Matlab, original complex model ka ek simplified version banao, jo zyada explainable ho, aur usi se samjho ki original model kya kar raha hai. Ise model distillation bhi kehte hain.

Surrogate model kya hai?

  • Surrogate model post-hoc explainability aur intrinsic interpretable models ke beech ka rasta hai.
  • Surrogate usually linear, decision tree, ya rule-based architecture hoti hai — inhe dekh kar seedha samajh aata hai ki model kya kar raha hai.
  • Ye original model ki architecture ko observe karke explanatory power deta hai.

Tradeoff — muft me kuch nahi milta

  • Performance kam: surrogate model ka performance almost hamesha original se worse hota hai.
  • Guarantee nahi: ye guarantee nahi de sakta ki saari predictions accurately explain ho rahi hain — khaas taur par edge cases ya training me under-represented areas me.
  • Research stage: automated model distillation abhi zyada research labs me hai, industry me kam. Iska matlab hai ki tumhe aksar apne techniques khud banane padenge, ya proof-of-concepts adapt karne padenge.
Interview me: "Surrogate model kab use karoge?" — Jab tumhe model ka global behaviour samajhna ho aur thodi accuracy ka tradeoff acceptable ho. Lekin critical decisions (healthcare, finance) me surrogate ki explanation par blind trust mat karo — woh original model ki poori kahani nahi batata.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — An Overview of Explainability
← Prev01.10 · Saliency Maps and Feature Attributions→ Next01.12 · Activation — Model ke andar kya "jalta" hai?
01.12Part I · Overview · Chapter 1

Activation — Model ke andar kya "jalta" hai?

Feature attribution batata hai ki kaunse features ne prediction ko influence kiya. Activation methods batati hain ki model ki architecture ke kaunse hisse ne prediction ko influence kiya.

Activation methods kya dekhti hain?

  • DNN me: kaunsi layers classification ke liye sabse pivotal thi, ya individual neurons ne final output me kitna contribute kiya.
  • Concepts: kuch techniques ye samajhne ki koshish karti hain ki model ne kaunse concepts seekhe hain — kisi input ke liye architecture ke andar kya activate hua.
  • Training influence: training ke dauraan, ek individual data point sirf kuch circumstances me active hota hai aur kuch labels ko strongly contribute karta hai — ye training influence kehlata hai, jo architecture ke andar activations ke analogous hai.

Concept Activation Vectors (CAV) — aage ki jhalak

Activation methods explainability ki sabse nayi techniques me se hain. Ye complex model ke internal state ko leverage karke uske behaviour ko samajhne ka intriguing tareeka deti hain.

  • Concept Activation Vectors (CAVs) Chapter 6 me discuss hote hain — ye batate hain ki model ne koi concept (jaise "stripes" ya "red colour") kitna seekha hai, aur woh concept prediction ko kaise influence karta hai.
  • Adoption abhi kam hai: ye techniques practitioners me abhi widely adopt nahi hui hain, isliye is book me inke applications kam dikhenge — lekin ye future ka direction hai.
Farak samjho: Attribution = "input ke kaunse features matter karte hain". Activation = "model ke andar kaunse neurons/layers matter karte hain". Dono mil kar poori picture dete hain — bahar se kya gaya, aur andar kya hua.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — An Overview of Explainability
← Prev01.11 · Surrogate Models — Model ka "duplicate" bana kar samjho→ Next01.13 · Putting It All Together — Sahi technique kaise chunein?
01.13Part I · Overview · Chapter 1

Putting It All Together — Sahi technique kaise chunein?

Explanations ki utility, meaning aur accuracy ke baare me sochna zaroori hai — lekin pehle ye samajhna ki explanations kis tarah vary karti hain, sahi tool chunne ka pehla step hai.

Technique chunne se pehle 3 sawaal

  1. Kaun receive kar raha hai explanation? — Practitioner, stakeholder, regulator, domain expert, ya affected user? Har audience ki needs alag hain.
  2. Kya explain karna hai? — Ek prediction? Poora model? Ek group? Features? Model ka andar ka hissa?
  3. Explanation ke baad kya hoga? — Koi action lena hai (model fix karna)? Bharosa banana hai? Fairness check karni hai? User ko recourse dena hai?

Do examples — sahi aur galat chunav

  • Loan deny hua (end-user): Global explanation jo model ki architecture samjhaye — bilkul irrelevant aur non-actionable. Behtar: local, feature-focused technique, jo user ke control wale factors par focus kare. Aur ek counterfactual bhi do: "agar aapka credit score aur finances doosre consumers jaise hote, to loan approve hone ki sambhavna hoti."
  • Business stakeholders: Inhe big picture chahiye — kaunse features globally influential hain? Ye complex, opaque model pichle linear model se zyada bharosemand kyun hai? Yahan global feature attribution technique (post-hoc, model-agnostic) use karke dono models ko compare karo.
Book ki sabse badi warning: Technique ko sirf isliye mat chuno kyunki try karne par explanation "achhi lagti hai". Bahut si techniques try karna jab tak koi explanation achhi na lage — ye sadak par mile 10 ajnabiyon se investment advice lene jaisa hai. Bahut si interesting opinions milengi, lekin zyada tar valid nahi hongi. Pehle audience, scope aur action tay karo, phir technique chuno.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — An Overview of Explainability
← Prev01.12 · Activation — Model ke andar kya "jalta" hai?→ Next02 · Integrated Gradients — Image Explainability ki shuruaat
02Part II · Image Data · Chapter 2

Integrated Gradients — Image Explainability ki shuruaat

Images 1980s se neural networks ke saath chali aa rahi hain — pehla famous example hai Yann LeCun ka handwritten digit recognition jo US Postal Service ne use kiya tha. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) aaj image classification aur segmentation ka best-performing architecture hain, aur image models ke liye explainability techniques back-propagation, perturbation, ya internal-state approaches use karti hain — ya inka combination.

Integrated Gradients (IG) — pehla successful approach

Integrated Gradients, Sundararajan et al. ka kaam, image explainability ka pehla successful approach tha. Ye local attribution technique hai jo gradient-based approach use karti hai.

  • Input: ek trained image model aur ek input image.
  • Output: ek saliency mask — ek overlay jo sabse zyada contribute karne wale pixels highlight karta hai.
  • Kaise kaam karta hai: technique ek "blank" baseline image se shuru karti hai, aur gradually input image ki taraf badhti hai (interpolation). Har step par model ka gradient calculate hota hai, aur saare gradients accumulate hote hain — wahi per-pixel attribution banta hai.
  • Baselines: black, white, ya Gaussian-noise images common hain (details aage).
  • Pros: kisi bhi differentiable model par kaam karta hai; implement karna easy hai (TensorFlow ke saath); low-contrast ya X-ray images ke liye bhi achha hai.
  • Cons: model differentiable hona chahiye aur gradients accessible hone chahiye; baseline aur hyperparameters ke prati sensitive hai.

Cockatoo example — "aha!" moment

Book me ek sulfur-crested cockatoo ki photo use ki gayi hai. Jab image ko black baseline se input image ki taraf interpolate karte hain:

  • Alpha 0.0–0.1: gradients lagbhag zero rehte hain — model ne bird ko abhi "dekha" hi nahi. Image me saara darkness cockatoo ka beak, jo pehle se hi black hai.
  • Alpha ~0.15: ek sudden change — gradients explode ho jate hain. Ye woh point hai jahan model ko lagta hai: "aha! Ye cockatoo hai!" — aur confidence bahut tezi se badhta hai.
  • Alpha 0.2 ke baad: gradient lagbhag constant ho jata hai — model ki confidence 0.98 se zyada hai aur saturate ho gayi hai.

Ye gradient saturation hai — model ko sirf chhota sa hissa dekh kar hi kaafi information mil jati hai, aur baaki image uski confidence ko zyada nahi badhati. Yehi wajah hai ki IG gradients ko accumulate karta hai — sirf final gradient lene se kuch pixels ka contribution miss ho jata.

Yaad rakho: IG ka core idea hai — baseline se input tak ka path, har step par gradient, aur unka sum. Agar model ko input ka sirf ek hissa dekh kar hi confidence aa jati hai, to gradient saturate ho jata hai — isliye accumulation zaroori hai, sirf ek gradient nahi.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Explainability for Image Data
← Prev01.13 · Putting It All Together — Sahi technique kaise chunein?→ Next02.1 · Choosing a Baseline — Baseline kyun matter karta hai?
02.1Part II · Image Data · Chapter 2

Choosing a Baseline — Baseline kyun matter karta hai?

Chapter 1 me humne baseline ko "neutral ya uninformative value" kaha tha. Images ke liye baseline ka matlab hai — ek aisi image jo model ko koi information nahi deti. Lekin "koi information nahi" ka matlab har image ke liye alag hota hai.

Common baselines

  • Black image: sab pixels zero. Sabse common baseline — "kuch nahi dikh raha" ka natural representation.
  • White image: sab pixels maximum. Kuch cases me better, lekin savdhaan — white image me bhi information ho sakti hai (aage dekho).
  • Gaussian-noise image: random noise. Model ke liye uninformative, lekin har run me alag result de sakta hai.

Baselines sirf colours nahi — paths bhi hote hain

Baseline se input tak ka path bhi matter karta hai — luminosity, saturation, ya blur ke through:

  • Luminosity path: image ko dheere-dheere bright karna — black se input tak.
  • Saturation path: grayscale se full colour tak.
  • Blur path: blurred image se sharp image tak — ye Blur-IG ka basis hai (section 02.4).

Doosre domains me baselines

  • Form template: agar model form images classify karta hai, to blank form template baseline ho sakta hai.
  • Empty assembly line: manufacturing defect detection me, khali assembly line ki image baseline ho sakti hai — taaki model sirf defect par focus kare, background par nahi.
  • Tabular data: har feature ke liye ek neutral value (jaise median ya mean) — Chapter 3 me details.
Interview tip: "Baseline kya hai?" ka jawab sirf "black image" nahi hai. Sahi jawab: ek aisi image jo model ko koi information nahi deti, aur jo input image ke context me neutral ho. Galat baseline = galat attribution — yehi Chapter 2 ka sabse bada lesson hai.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Explainability for Image Data
← Prev02 · Integrated Gradients — Image Explainability ki shuruaat→ Next02.2 · Accumulating Gradients — IG ko code me kaise karein?
02.2Part II · Image Data · Chapter 2

Accumulating Gradients — IG ko code me kaise karein?

IG ka idea simple hai, lekin implementation me kuch details hain — interpolation, gradient accumulation, aur ek delta check jo batata hai ki tumne kaafi steps liye ya nahi. Book me TensorFlow ka code diya gaya hai.

Step 1: Interpolate — baseline se input tak

interpolate_images — baseline se input tak ka path

Book me diya gaya complete code (jaisa printed hai).

def interpolate_images(baseline,
image,
alphas):
alphas_x = alphas[:, tf.newaxis, tf.newaxis, tf.newaxis]
baseline_x = tf.expand_dims(baseline, axis=0)
input_x = tf.expand_dims(image, axis=0)
images = alphas_x * input_x + (1 - alphas_x) * baseline_x
return images

Step 2: Softmax prediction — model kya kehta hai?

pred_softmax — model ki prediction
LABEL = 'sulfur-crested cockatoo'
pred = model(interpolated_images)
idx_cockatoo = np.where(imagenet_labels==LABEL)[0][0]
pred_proba = tf.nn.softmax(pred, axis=-1)[:, idx_cockatoo]

Step 3: Gradients compute karo — TensorFlow GradientTape

compute_gradients — har step par gradient
def compute_gradients(images, target_class_idx):
with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
tape.watch(images)
logits = model(images)
probs = tf.nn.softmax(logits, axis=-1)[:, target_class_idx]
return tape.gradient(probs, images)

Step 4: Delta check — kya steps kaafi the?

IG ka ek built-in quality check hai: delta — accumulated gradients ka sum aur actual prediction difference ke beech ka farak. Agar |delta| > 0.05 hai, to steps badhao.

delta_check — approximation error check karo
# The baseline's prediction and attribution score
baseline_prediction = model(tf.expand_dims(baseline, 0))
baseline_score = tf.nn.softmax(tf.squeeze(baseline_prediction))[target_class_idx]
# Your model's prediction and attribution score
input_prediction = model(tf.expand_dims(input, 0))
input_score = tf.nn.softmax(tf.squeeze(input_prediction))[target_class_idx]
# Compare with the attribution score from integrated gradients
ig_score = tf.math.reduce_sum(attributions)
delta = ig_score - (input_score - baseline_score)
  • m_steps: 20–300 suggest kiya gaya hai; shuruaat 10–30 se karo, phir delta dekh kar badhao.
  • Riemann sums: IG gradients ko path ke along integrate karta hai — Riemann sum se approximate karta hai. Zyada steps = behtar approximation, zyada compute.
  • Gradient saturation: cockatoo example me alpha > 0.2 ke baad gradients saturate ho gaye — model ki confidence 0.98+ thi aur badh nahi rahi thi. Isliye accumulation zaroori hai.

Step 5: IG function — sab kuch ek saath

ig_function — poora Integrated Gradients
# Generate alphas.
alphas = tf.linspace(start=0.0, stop=1.0, num=m_steps+1)
# Collect gradients.
gradient_batches = []
# Iterate alphas range and batch speed, efficiency, and scaling
for alpha in tf.range(0, len(alphas), batch_size):
from_ = alpha
to = tf.minimum(from_ + batch_size, len(alphas))
alpha_batch = alphas[from_:to]
gradient_batch = one_batch(baseline, image, alpha_batch, target_class_idx)
gradient_batches.append(gradient_batch)
# Concatenate path gradients.
total_gradients = tf.concat(gradient_batches, axis=0)
# Compute Integral approximation of all gradients.
avg_gradients = integral_approximation(gradients=total_gradients)
# Scale integrated gradients with respect to input.
integrated_gradients = (image - baseline) * avg_gradients

Step 6: Attribution mask — pixels ko dikhao

attr_mask — attribution se saliency mask
attributions = integrated_gradients(baseline=black_baseline,
image=input_image,
target_class_idx=target_class_idx,
m_steps=m_steps)
attribution_mask = tf.reduce_sum(tf.math.abs(attributions), axis=-1)
  • Result: original image + mask → overlay. Mask me bright areas woh pixels hain jo prediction me sabse zyada contribute karte hain.
  • PAIR library: book me saliency library ka istemal dikhaya gaya hai — mask banane aur visualize karne ke liye.
Practical tip: m_steps ko blindly 300 mat rakho — pehle 20 se shuru karo, delta check karo, aur sirf zaroorat padne par badhao. Har step ek forward+backward pass hai — compute cost seedha steps se multiply hota hai.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Explainability for Image Data
← Prev02.1 · Choosing a Baseline — Baseline kyun matter karta hai?→ Next02.3 · Baselines Matter — White baseline ka dhokha
02.3Part II · Image Data · Chapter 2

Baselines Matter — White baseline ka dhokha

Baselines Matter — ye section ka title hi warning hai. Ek galat baseline explanation ko poori tarah badal sakta hai, aur tumhe pata bhi nahi chalega.

White cockatoo + white baseline = problem

Sulfur-crested cockatoo white hai. Agar baseline white image hai, to:

  • White baseline me pehle se hi information hai — white pixels cockatoo ke white feathers se match karte hain.
  • Result: attribution mask bilkul alag aata hai — black baseline se mile mask se compare karo to farak saaf dikhta hai.
  • Lesson: baseline "neutral" hona chahiye — input image ke context me. White bird ke liye white baseline neutral nahi hai.

Sahi baseline kaise chunein?

  • Black baseline: zyada tar cases me safe — "kuch nahi dikh raha".
  • Domain-specific baseline: form template, empty assembly line — jo input ke context me "kuch nahi" ho.
  • Multiple baselines try karo: agar do alag baselines se attribution bilkul alag aata hai, to ye ek signal hai ki explanation baseline-sensitive hai — aur tumhe ye stakeholders ko batana chahiye.
  • Gaussian noise: kabhi-kabhi useful, lekin har run me alag result — reproducibility ke liye seed fix karo.
Yaad rakho: Baseline ka chunav explanation ka hissa hai — ye ek hyperparameter hai, aur iski sensitivity ko document karna chahiye. Interview me ye point bahut strong hai: "IG baseline-sensitive hai, isliye main multiple baselines se cross-check karta hun."
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Explainability for Image Data
← Prev02.2 · Accumulating Gradients — IG ko code me kaise karein?→ Next02.4 · Blur-IG — Blurred image ko baseline banao
02.4Part II · Image Data · Chapter 2

Blur-IG — Blurred image ko baseline banao

Blur-IG ek variation hai jo baseline ki problem ko ek clever tareeke se solve karta hai: baseline ke roop me ek blurred version of the input image use karo.

Blur-IG kaise kaam karta hai?

  • Baseline: input image ka Gaussian-blurred version — ye image ki broad structure rakhta hai, lekin fine details hata deta hai.
  • Path: blurred image se sharp image tak — blur ko dheere-dheere kam karte hue.
  • Gaussian blur variance: ye ek hyperparameter hai — kitna blur karna hai, ye tune karna padta hai.
  • Goldfinch example: jab goldfinch ki image ko blur kiya gaya, to model ne use 'safety pin' predict kiya (97.5% confidence ke saath) — kyunki blur hone par bird ka shape safety pin jaisa lagne laga. Ye dikhata hai ki model fine details par kitna depend karta hai.

Kab use karein Blur-IG?

  • Jab black/white baseline input ke context me neutral nahi hai.
  • Jab tumhe ye samajhna hai ki model fine details par kitna depend karta hai vs broad structure par.
  • Pros: baseline input se hi banta hai, isliye context-aware hai; blur ka level tune kar sakte ho.
  • Cons: blur variance ek aur hyperparameter hai; har image ke liye best blur alag ho sakta hai.
Insight: Goldfinch → safety pin wala example batata hai ki model ka "understanding" humare jaisa nahi hai. Hum bird dekhte hain, model shapes aur textures dekhta hai. Blur-IG ye difference dikhane ka achha tareeka hai.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Explainability for Image Data
← Prev02.3 · Baselines Matter — White baseline ka dhokha→ Next02.5 · Guided IG — Behtar path chuno
02.5Part II · Image Data · Chapter 2

Guided IG — Behtar path chuno

Standard IG ek seedha (straight-line) path follow karta hai baseline se input tak. Lekin ye path hamesha best nahi hota — kuch regions me gradients saturated ya noisy ho sakte hain. Guided IG path ko adapt karta hai.

Guided IG ka idea

  • Adapted path: har step par woh direction chuno jisme partial derivatives sabse chhote hain — matlab, woh rasta jahan gradient sabse kam "shor" karta hai.
  • Kyunki: saturated ya noisy regions se guzarna attribution ko bigaad deta hai. Guided IG un regions se bach kar chalta hai.
  • Result: cleaner, zyada focused attribution masks — khaas taur par jab standard IG noisy ho.

Lekin koi one-size-fits-all nahi

Book ek honest note deti hai: neither IG nor Guided IG does a great job on the goldfinch — goldfinch example me dono hi techniques perfect explanation nahi deti hain.

  • Har technique ki limitations hain — koi bhi technique har image, har model, har case me best nahi hoti.
  • Isliye: multiple techniques try karo, unhe compare karo, aur limitations ko stakeholders ko saaf batao.
  • Yehi wajah hai ki Chapter 7 (Choosing the Right Technique) itna important hai — technique chunna ek decision hai, na ki ek default.
Yaad rakho: Guided IG ka path "smart" hai, lekin ye bhi perfect nahi hai. Technique ki limitations ko jaanna, technique ko jaanne se zyada important hai.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Explainability for Image Data
← Prev02.4 · Blur-IG — Blurred image ko baseline banao→ Next02.6 · XRAI — Region-based attribution
02.6Part II · Image Data · Chapter 2

XRAI — Region-based attribution

XRAI (eXplanation with Ranked Area Integrals) ek region-based technique hai jo Integrated Gradients par banayi gayi hai. Pixel-level attribution ki jagah, ye regions ki attribution deti hai — jo insaan ko samajhne me zyada aasan hoti hai.

XRAI kaise kaam karta hai?

  • Step 1 — IG: pehle Integrated Gradients se per-pixel attribution nikalo.
  • Step 2 — Segmentation: image ko Felzenszwalb segmentation se regions me baanto — similar pixels ek saath group hote hain.
  • Step 3 — Graph + MST: regions ko graph ke nodes banao, aur Kruskal's algorithm se Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) banao — regions ko unke similarity ke hisaab se jodo.
  • Step 4 — Ranked areas: har region ka attribution uske pixels ke IG attributions ka sum hai. Regions ko attribution ke hisaab se rank karo.
  • k parameter: [50, 100, 150, 250, 500, 1200] — kitne regions dikhane hain, ye control karta hai. Default steps = 100.
  • Small segments: 20 pixels se chhote segments ignore kar diye jate hain.
  • Over-segmentation: ~6× over-segmentation hoti hai — matlab, regions zyada chhote bante hain, phir unhe merge kiya jata hai.

Pros aur Cons

  • Pros: IG se behtar (region-level, zyada interpretable); LIME se faster; natural images par best performance.
  • Cons: sirf images ke liye; IG se kam granular (pixel-level detail nahi); low-contrast ya X-ray images ke liye achha nahi.
  • Library: saliency library me XRAIParameters aur XRAI available hain.

Code — XRAI setup aur call

xrai_setup — XRAI parameters aur model setup
m = tf.keras.applications.vgg16.VGG16(weights='imagenet', include_top=True)
conv_layer = m.get_layer('block5_conv3')
model = tf.keras.models.Model([m.inputs], [conv_layer.output, m.output])
xrai_object = saliency.XRAI()
xrai_attributions = xrai_object.GetMask(image,
call_model_function,
call_model_args,
batch_size=20)
xrai_callfn — XRAI call function
class_idx_str = 'class_idx_str'
def call_model_function(images, call_model_args=None, expected_keys=None):
target_class_idx = call_model_args[class_idx_str]
images = tf.convert_to_tensor(images)
with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
if expected_keys==[saliency.base.INPUT_OUTPUT_GRADIENTS]:
tape.watch(images)
_, output_layer = model(images)
output_layer = output_layer[:,target_class_idx]
gradients = np.array(tape.gradient(output_layer, images))
return {saliency.base.INPUT_OUTPUT_GRADIENTS: gradients}
else:
conv_layer, output_layer = model(images)
gradients = np.array(tape.gradient(output_layer, conv_layer))
return {saliency.base.CONVOLUTION_LAYER_VALUES: conv_layer,
saliency.base.CONVOLUTION_OUTPUT_GRADIENTS: gradients}
xrai_params — XRAI parameters (steps, k)
xrai_params = saliency.XRAIParameters()
xrai_params.steps = 200
xrai_attributions_fast = xrai_object.GetMask(im,
call_model_function,
call_model_args,
extra_parameters=xrai_params,
batch_size=20)
Yaad rakho: XRAI ka "k" parameter ek slider jaisa hai — kam k = sirf top regions, zyada k = zyada detail. Lab L4 me tum ye slider khud try kar sakte ho.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Explainability for Image Data
← Prev02.5 · Guided IG — Behtar path chuno→ Next02.7 · Grad-CAM — Class Activation Mapping, gradient se
02.7Part II · Image Data · Chapter 2

Grad-CAM — Class Activation Mapping, gradient se

Grad-CAM (Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping) image explainability ki sabse popular technique hai — kyunki ye forward-pass only hai, fast hai, aur kisi bhi CNN par kaam karti hai.

CAM se Grad-CAM tak

  • CAM (Class Activation Mapping): original technique — lekin iske liye model architecture specific honi chahiye: conv layer → Global Average Pooling (GAP) → softmax. Har model aisa nahi hota.
  • Grad-CAM: CAM ko generalize karta hai — kisi bhi CNN par kaam karta hai, architecture change kiye bina. Gradients use karke importance weights nikalta hai.

Grad-CAM kaise kaam karta hai?

  • Final conv layer: VGG-16 me final conv layer 7×7×512 hai — 512 feature maps, har ek 7×7.
  • Importance weights (alpha): har feature map ke liye ek weight — target class ke score ka gradient, us feature map ke respect me, globally average kiya gaya.
  • Weighted sum + ReLU: feature maps ko unke weights se multiply karke sum karo, phir ReLU lagao — sirf positive contributions rakho.
  • Upsample: result 7×7 ka coarse heatmap hota hai, use 224×224 tak upsample karke original image par overlay karo.
  • Classes: ImageNet me 1,000 classes hain — Grad-CAM kisi bhi ek class ke liye heatmap bana sakta hai.
WARNING — book ki sabse badi chetavni: Grad-CAM ka heatmap coarse aur misleading ho sakta hai. 7×7 se 224×224 tak upsampling karne par heatmap blurry hota hai, aur ye galat jagah highlight kar sakta hai. Blueberry leaf example (Fig 2-22) me ye dikhta hai. Grad-CAM++ aur HiResCAM is problem ko fix karte hain — behtar resolution aur zyada accurate localization ke saath.

Pros aur Cons

  • Pros: sirf forward pass chahiye (fast, efficient); kisi bhi CNN par kaam karta hai; implement karna easy hai.
  • Cons: heatmaps galat/misleading ho sakte hain; multi-class (bahut saare labels) ke liye achha nahi; ek hi class ke multiple objects hone par fail ho sakta hai; low resolution (7×7).

Code — Grad-CAM

gradcam — Grad-CAM implementation

Book me diya gaya complete code (jaisa printed hai).

vgg16 = tf.keras.applications.vgg16.VGG16(
weights='imagenet', include_top=True)
conv_layer = m.get_layer('block5_conv3')
model = tf.keras.models.Model(
[vgg16.inputs], [conv_layer.output, vgg16.output])
grad_cam = saliency.GradCam()
# Compute the Grad-CAM mask.
grad_cam_mask_3d = grad_cam.GetMask(im, call_model_function,
call_model_args)
Interview tip: "Grad-CAM kab use karoge aur kab nahi?" — Use karo jab tumhe fast, coarse localization chahiye (debugging, demo). Mat use karo jab tumhe precise, trustworthy localization chahiye (medical, safety-critical) — wahan Grad-CAM++ ya HiResCAM, ya IG/XRAI behtar hain.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Explainability for Image Data
← Prev02.6 · XRAI — Region-based attribution→ Next02.8 · LIME — Model-agnostic, perturbation-based
02.8Part II · Image Data · Chapter 2

LIME — Model-agnostic, perturbation-based

LIME (Locally Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations) explainability ki sabse popular aur sabse zyada cite ki jaane wali technique hai. Ye model-agnostic hai — kisi bhi model par kaam karti hai, kyunki ye model ke andar nahi dekhti, sirf uske inputs aur outputs ko observe karti hai.

LIME kaise kaam karta hai? — 4 steps

  1. Segment karo: image ko superpixels me baanto — quickshift algorithm se (kernel_size=4, max_dist=200, ratio=0.2). Superpixels woh regions hain jo visually similar hain.
  2. Perturb karo: kuch superpixels ko "gray out" karo ya unhe mean value se replace karo — bahut saare perturbed versions banao.
  3. Predict karo: har perturbed version ko model se predict karwao.
  4. Local model train karo: perturbed examples par ek simple, interpretable model (linear model) train karo, har example ko original image se proximity ke hisaab se weight de kar. Is local model ke coefficients hi explanation hain — kaunsa superpixel prediction ko kitna influence karta hai.

Visualization — green aur red

  • Green = positive: woh superpixels jo prediction ko support karte hain.
  • Red = negative: woh superpixels jo prediction ke against jate hain.
  • Parameters: LimeImageExplainer, top_labels=20, hide_color=0, num_features=5, get_image_and_mask with positive_only.

LIME ki problems — book bahut honest hai

  • Brittle hai: chhoti si change se explanation badal sakti hai — reproducibility kam hai.
  • Background ko influential samajh leta hai: goldfinch example me LIME ne background ko important bataya, jabki bird hi main subject tha. PlantVillage leaf example me bhi background highlight hua.
  • Slow hai: bahut saare model queries chahiye (har perturbed version ke liye ek prediction) — large models par mehenga.
  • Nonsensical explanations: kabhi-kabhi aisi explanations deti hai jo insaan ko bilkul sense nahi banati — jaise models "Schuler" (99.8% accurate) aur "Yosuke" ke cases me.

Code — LIME segmentation aur implementation

lime_seg — superpixel segmentation (quickshift)
from skimage.segmentation import quickshift
segments = quickshift(im_orig, kernel_size=4,
max_dist=200, ratio=0.2)
lime_impl — LIME explainer aur mask

Book me diya gaya complete code (jaisa printed hai).

inception = tf.keras.applications.InceptionV3(
include_top=True, weights='imagenet')
model = tf.keras.models.Model(inception.inputs, inception.output)
explainer = lime_image.LimeImageExplainer()
explanation = explainer.explain_instance(image.astype('double'),
inception.predict,
top_labels=20,
hide_color=0,
num_features=5)
temp, mask = explanation.get_image_and_mask(explanation.top_labels[0],
positive_only=True,
num_features=20,
hide_rest=True)
plt.imshow(mark_boundaries(temp, mask))
Yaad rakho: LIME popular hai kyunki ye easy aur intuitive hai — lekin "popular" ka matlab "reliable" nahi hai. Interview me LIME ki limitations batana (brittle, slow, background problem) tumhe alag karta hai — kyunki zyada log sirf uske fayde batate hain.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Explainability for Image Data
← Prev02.7 · Grad-CAM — Class Activation Mapping, gradient se→ Next02.9 · Guided Backpropagation aur Guided Grad-CAM
02.9Part II · Image Data · Chapter 2

Guided Backpropagation aur Guided Grad-CAM

Guided Backpropagation aur Guided Grad-CAM do techniques hain jo backpropagation ko modify karke sharper, zyada detailed saliency maps banati hain. Lekin inki ek badi problem hai — ye sanity checks fail karti hain.

DeConvNets — shuruaat kahan se hui?

  • DeConvNets (Deconvolutional Networks): CNN ke ulta — transposed convolution + unpooling (switch variables ke saath) use karke, ye batate hain ki model ne kya "dekha".
  • DeConvNet ka rule: sirf positive signals ko backpropagate karo — negative gradients ko rok do.
  • Guided Backprop: DeConvNet se ek kadam aage — sirf positive signals hi nahi, balki sirf woh signals jo forward pass me bhi positive the. Matlab, gradient tabhi pass hoga jab input bhi positive tha aur gradient bhi positive tha. Result: bahut sharper, zyada detailed maps.

Guided Grad-CAM — dono ka combination

Guided Grad-CAM = Grad-CAM × Guided Backprop (element-wise product).

  • Grad-CAM batata hai "kahan" — coarse localization (7×7 heatmap).
  • Guided Backprop batata hai "kya detail" — fine-grained, sharp map.
  • Product: dono ko multiply karne se ek high-resolution, class-discriminative map milta hai — Grad-CAM ki localization + Guided Backprop ki detail.
  • Captum: GuidedBackprop aur GuidedGradCam (model.Mixed_7c layer ke saath) — PyTorch Captum library me available hain.
WARNING — Adebayo et al. sanity checks (2020): "Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps" paper ne dikhaya ki Guided Backprop aur Guided Grad-CAM model parameters aur training data ko randomize karne par bhi zyada nahi badalte — matlab, ye maps model se zyada, input image ki structure ko reflect karte hain. Agar model ke weights random hain aur phir bhi wahi map aa raha hai, to woh map model ke baare me kuch nahi bata raha! Ye explainability ki sabse badi warning hai — ek achhi dikhne wali explanation ka matlab ye nahi ki woh sahi hai.

Code — Guided Backprop aur Guided Grad-CAM (Captum)

guided — GuidedBackprop aur GuidedGradCam

Book me diya gaya complete code (jaisa printed hai). Captum library use hoti hai.

import torch
model = torch.hub.load('pytorch/vision:v0.10.0',
'inception_v3',
pretrained=True)
model.eval()
gbp = GuidedBackprop(model)
# Computes Guided Backprop attribution scores for class 89 (cockatoo)
attribution = gbp.attribute(input_batch, target=top5_catid[0])
from captum.attr import GuidedGradCam
guided_gc = GuidedGradCam(model, model.Mixed_7c)
attribution = guided_gc.attribute(input_batch, target=top5_catid[0])

Chapter 2 Summary — categories yaad rakho

Chapter 2 ki techniques 4 categories me aati hain:

  • Back-propagation: Integrated Gradients, Blur-IG, Guided IG, Grad-CAM, Guided Backprop, Guided Grad-CAM.
  • Perturbation: LIME (inputs badal kar dekho).
  • Internal-state: (Chapter 6 me CAVs ke saath aur gehrai se).
  • Combinations: XRAI (IG + segmentation), Guided Grad-CAM (Grad-CAM + Guided Backprop).
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — Explainability for Image Data
← Prev02.8 · LIME — Model-agnostic, perturbation-based→ Next03 · Explainability for Tabular Data — Aage kya hai
03Part III · Aage ke Chapters · Chapter 3

Explainability for Tabular Data — Aage kya hai

Important note: Ye section is Early Release PDF me nahi hai — ye overview sirf book ke andar ke cross-references se banaya gaya hai, taaki tumhe pata ho ki aage kya aane wala hai. Final published book me ye chapter poora milega.

Tabular data — spreadsheets, databases, CSV files — ML ka sabse common data type hai. Loan approval, churn prediction, fraud detection — sab tabular data par chalte hain. Chapter 3 isi par focus karta hai.

Chapter 3 me kya aayega? (book ke references se)

  • Shapley values (tabular): Chapter 1 me jo Shapley values seekhe, woh tabular data par sabse zyada use hote hain — har feature ka attribution, har row ke liye.
  • Permutation feature importance: ek feature ki values ko shuffle karke dekho — model ki performance kitni girti hai? Jitni zyada girawat, utna important feature.
  • Tree interpreters: decision trees aur random forests ke liye specific techniques — tree ke andar kaise decisions hote hain, ye dikhana.
  • Partial dependence plots (PDP): ek feature ko badalne par prediction kaise badalta hai — baaki features ko average karke. Ye global behaviour samajhne ka powerful tareeka hai.
  • Baselines (tabular): har feature ke liye neutral value kya hogi — median, mean, ya domain-specific value? Chapter 1 me baselines ka concept yahan practical hota hai.

Tabular vs Image — kya alag hai?

  • Tabular features ke naam aur matlab hote hain (age, income, credit score) — isliye attribution ko samajhna aasan hai.
  • Features correlated ho sakte hain — isliye attribution ko interpret karte waqt correlation ka dhyaan rakhna padta hai.
  • Baseline chunna images se alag hai — "blank" ka matlab tabular me kya hai, ye domain par depend karta hai.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 3 — Explainability for Tabular Data
← Prev02.9 · Guided Backpropagation aur Guided Grad-CAM→ Next04 · Explainability for NLP — Aage kya hai
04Part III · Aage ke Chapters · Chapter 5

Explainability for NLP — Aage kya hai

Important note: Ye section is Early Release PDF me nahi hai — ye overview sirf book ke andar ke cross-references se banaya gaya hai, taaki tumhe pata ho ki aage kya aane wala hai. Final published book me ye chapter poora milega.

NLP models — text classification, sentiment analysis, question answering — aaj har jagah hain. Chapter 5 batata hai ki text models ko kaise explain karein.

Chapter 5 me kya aayega? (book ke references se)

  • Token attribution: kaunse words ya tokens ne prediction ko sabse zyada influence kiya? Image me pixels ki tarah, text me tokens hote hain.
  • Gradient techniques (text): Integrated Gradients text models par bhi apply hota hai — lekin baseline kya hogi? Ek "blank" token, ya padding token?
  • Attention: Transformer models me attention weights batate hain ki model kis word par dhyaan de raha hai — lekin attention = explanation nahi hai (ye ek controversial topic hai).
  • LIME (text): words ko hata kar ya badal kar dekho — prediction kaise badalta hai? LIME text par bhi kaam karta hai.
  • Baselines (text): ek "neutral" text kya hota hai? Empty string? Padding? Ye Chapter 1 ke baseline concept ka text version hai.

Text vs Image — kya alag hai?

  • Text discrete hai — words ko "thoda sa" badal nahi sakte, sirf replace kar sakte ho. Isliye interpolation (IG ka core) text me mushkil hai.
  • Words ka order matter karta hai — "dog bites man" aur "man bites dog" alag hain.
  • Attribution ko samajhna aasan hai — kyunki words ke matlab hote hain, pixels ki tarah nahi.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 5 — Explainability for NLP
← Prev03 · Explainability for Tabular Data — Aage kya hai→ Next05 · Advanced Techniques — Concept Activation Vectors
05Part III · Aage ke Chapters · Chapter 6

Advanced Techniques — Concept Activation Vectors

Important note: Ye section is Early Release PDF me nahi hai — ye overview sirf book ke andar ke cross-references se banaya gaya hai, taaki tumhe pata ho ki aage kya aane wala hai. Final published book me ye chapter poora milega.

Concept Activation Vectors (CAVs) explainability ki sabse advanced aur exciting techniques me se hain. Ye Chapter 1 me discuss ki gayi activation methods ka practical roop hain.

CAVs kya hain? (book ke references se)

  • Concept: ek human-understandable idea — jaise "stripes", "red colour", "doctor's handwriting" — jo model ne seekha ho.
  • CAV: ek vector jo model ke andar us concept ki direction batata hai — kaunsi neurons/layers us concept ko represent karti hain.
  • TCAV (Testing with CAVs): ye test karta hai ki ek concept prediction ko kitna influence karta hai — jaise "stripes" concept zebra prediction ko kitna affect karta hai?
  • Kyunki: ye feature attribution se ek kadam aage hai — ye batata hai ki model ne kya seekha, sirf ye nahi ki kaunsa input important tha.

Abhi adoption kyun kam hai?

  • CAVs ke liye concept examples chahiye — har concept ke liye alag dataset banana padta hai.
  • Technique abhi research stage me hai — industry me widely adopt nahi hui.
  • Lekin ye future ka direction hai — Chapter 8 me is par aur charcha hai.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 6 — Advanced Techniques — Concept Activation Vectors
← Prev04 · Explainability for NLP — Aage kya hai→ Next06 · Choosing the Right Technique — Aage kya hai
06Part III · Aage ke Chapters · Chapter 7

Choosing the Right Technique — Aage kya hai

Important note: Ye section is Early Release PDF me nahi hai — ye overview sirf book ke andar ke cross-references se banaya gaya hai, taaki tumhe pata ho ki aage kya aane wala hai. Final published book me ye chapter poora milega.

Chapter 7 poori book ka sabse practical chapter hai — sahi technique kaise chunein? Chapter 1 ke 3 sawaal yahan ek decision framework bante hain.

Chapter 7 me kya aayega? (book ke references se)

  • Decision framework: audience (practitioner/stakeholder/end-user) + scope (local/global/cohort) + modality (tabular/image/text) + action (fix/trust/audit) → technique.
  • Technique comparison: IG vs LIME vs Grad-CAM vs XRAI vs SHAP — kab kaunsi, kyun, aur kya tradeoff hai?
  • Sanity checks: Adebayo et al. ke sanity checks jaise tests — explanation sahi hai ya sirf achhi dikh rahi hai, ye kaise verify karein?
  • Multiple techniques: ek hi technique par bharosa mat karo — cross-check karo, aur limitations document karo.

Chapter 1 se connection

Chapter 1 ke end me jo 3 sawaal diye gaye the (kaun receive kar raha hai? kya explain karna hai? explanation ke baad kya hoga?) — Chapter 7 unhi sawaalon ka detailed jawab hai, har technique ke pros/cons ke saath.

SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 7 — Choosing the Right Technique

07Part III · Aage ke Chapters · Chapter 8

Future of Explainability — Aage kya hai

Important note: Ye section is Early Release PDF me nahi hai — ye overview sirf book ke andar ke cross-references se banaya gaya hai, taaki tumhe pata ho ki aage kya aane wala hai. Final published book me ye chapter poora milega.

Explainability abhi ek young field hai — bahut kuch badalne wala hai. Chapter 8 future ki taraf dekhta hai.

Chapter 8 me kya aayega? (book ke references se)

  • Two-way explanations: aaj ki techniques one-way hain — model insaan ko explanation deta hai, lekin follow-up sawaal ka jawab nahi de sakta. Future me interactive, conversational explanations aayengi — jahan tum model se sawaal poochh sako.
  • CAVs aur activation methods: adoption badhega, aur ye techniques zyada practical hongi.
  • Fairness integration: explainability aur fairness ke underpinnings same hain — future me dono ko saath me dekha jayega.
  • Regulation: jaise-jaise AI regulation badhega (EU AI Act jaise), explainability ek legal requirement ban jayegi — sirf "nice to have" nahi.
  • Standardization: terms aur techniques ka standardize hona — taaki "explainability" ka matlab har jagah ek hi ho.
Yaad rakho: Ye book Early Release hai — final published book (Nov 2022) me Chapters 3–8 poore milenge. Is SPA me Part I aur Part II (Chapters 1–2) poori detail me hain, aur Part III me aage ke chapters ka overview hai — taaki tumhe poori picture mile.
SOURCESource: Explainable AI for Practitioners, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — Future of Explainability
