F1End Matter · Interview FAQs

Interview FAQs

XAI interviews (current era) ke liye — explainability ki buniyaad se lekar technique selection tak, 30 sawaal-jawaab. Har jawaab isi book ke concepts par aadharit hai.

Q01 Explainability aur interpretability me kya farak hai?
Explainability techniques hain jo prediction ke peeche ka reason batati hain (prediction ke basis par). Interpretability model khud kitna samajhne layak hai (architecture aur mechanism kitna transparent hai). Dono alag hain, lekin aksar interchangeably use hote hain — interview me ye farak poochha jata hai.
Q02 Shapley values kya hain aur ye kyun important hain?
Shapley values game theory se aaye hain (Lloyd Shapley, 1951, Nobel 2012). Ye features ke alag-alag groups (coalitions) ke saath predictions test karke har feature ka attribution nikalte hain. Inki sabse badi property hai Efficiency — Shapley values ka sum poori prediction ke barabar hota hai. Ye decades se use me hain aur academically well-studied hain.
Q03 Shapley values compute karna mushkil kyun hai?
Poori Shapley calculation ke liye 2^n combinations chahiye — 10 features ke liye 1,024 combinations. Isliye practically har technique Sampled Shapley use karti hai — kuch paths sample karke approximate karna. Tradeoff: zyada samples = kam error, zyada runtime.
Q04 Baseline kya hai aur ye kyun matter karta hai?
Baseline ek neutral ya uninformative value hai jo prediction ko influence nahi karti. Ye Shapley paths aur IG me partial predictions nikalne ke liye use hoti hai. Galat baseline = galat attribution. White bird ke liye white baseline galat hai kyunki white pixels bird se match karte hain. Baseline ka chunav explanation ka hissa hai.
Q05 Integrated Gradients (IG) kaise kaam karta hai?
IG ek baseline image se shuru karke input image ki taraf interpolate karta hai. Har step par model ka gradient calculate hota hai, aur saare gradients accumulate hote hain — wahi per-pixel attribution banta hai. Ye local attribution technique hai, kisi bhi differentiable model par kaam karti hai.
Q06 Gradient saturation kya hai?
Jab model ko input ka sirf chhota sa hissa dekh kar hi confidence aa jati hai, to gradient saturate ho jata hai — aur badhta nahi. Cockatoo example me alpha 0.2 ke baad gradient constant ho gaya kyunki confidence 0.98+ thi. Isliye IG gradients ko accumulate karta hai, sirf final gradient nahi leta.
Q07 IG me m_steps kitne rakhne chahiye?
Book 20–300 suggest karta hai; shuruaat 10–30 se karo. Delta check karo — agar |delta| > 0.05 hai, to steps badhao. Har step ek forward+backward pass hai, isliye zyada steps = zyada compute cost.
Q08 Delta check kya hai?
Delta accumulated gradients ka sum aur actual prediction difference ke beech ka farak hai. Ye IG approximation ki quality batata hai. Agar |delta| > 0.05 hai, to approximation achhi nahi hai — m_steps badhao.
Q09 Blur-IG kya hai?
Blur-IG me baseline input image ka Gaussian-blurred version hota hai. Path blurred se sharp image tak jata hai. Ye tab useful hai jab black/white baseline input ke context me neutral nahi hai. Goldfinch example me blurred image ko model ne "safety pin" predict kiya — ye dikhata hai ki model fine details par kitna depend karta hai.
Q10 Guided IG standard IG se kaise alag hai?
Standard IG baseline se input tak seedha path follow karta hai. Guided IG path ko adapt karta hai — har step par woh direction chunta hai jisme partial derivatives sabse chhote hain, taaki saturated ya noisy regions se bacha ja sake. Result cleaner masks hote hain, lekin ye bhi perfect nahi hai.
Q11 XRAI kya hai aur ye IG se kaise behtar hai?
XRAI (eXplanation with Ranked Area Integrals) IG par based region-based technique hai. Ye image ko Felzenszwalb segmentation se regions me baant ta hai, phir har region ka attribution uske pixels ke IG attributions ka sum hota hai. Ye IG se zyada interpretable hai (regions, pixels nahi), LIME se faster hai, aur natural images par best hai. Lekin ye sirf images ke liye hai aur low-contrast/X-ray ke liye achha nahi.
Q12 XRAI me k parameter kya hai?
k batata hai kitne regions dikhane hain — [50, 100, 150, 250, 500, 1200]. Kam k = sirf top regions (broad overview), zyada k = zyada detail. 20px se chhote segments ignore hote hain. Default steps = 100.
Q13 Grad-CAM kya hai?
Grad-CAM (Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping) ek technique hai jo kisi bhi CNN par kaam karti hai, bina architecture change kiye. Ye final conv layer ke feature maps ke importance weights gradients se nikalta hai, phir weighted sum + ReLU karke ek coarse heatmap banata hai (VGG-16 me 7×7), use upsample karke image par overlay karta hai. Ye forward-pass only hai, isliye fast hai.
Q14 Grad-CAM ki sabse badi problem kya hai?
Uska heatmap coarse aur misleading ho sakta hai — 7×7 se 224×224 tak upsampling karne par ye galat jagah highlight kar sakta hai. Ye multi-class aur multiple same-class objects par bhi fail ho sakta hai. Grad-CAM++ aur HiResCAM is problem ko fix karte hain.
Q15 Grad-CAM++ aur HiResCAM kya hain?
Ye Grad-CAM ke improved versions hain jo behtar resolution aur zyada accurate localization dete hain. Grad-CAM++ multiple same-class objects ko behtar handle karta hai, aur HiResCAM heatmap ki accuracy badhata hai. Medical ya safety-critical use cases me inhe prefer karo.
Q16 LIME kya hai?
LIME (Locally Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations) ek model-agnostic, perturbation-based technique hai. Ye image ko superpixels me baant ta hai, kuch superpixels ko gray out karke bahut saare perturbed versions banata hai, har version ko model se predict karwata hai, aur phir ek simple linear model train karke batata hai ki kaunsa superpixel prediction ko kitna influence karta hai.
Q17 LIME model-agnostic kyun hai?
Kyunki LIME model ke andar nahi dekhta — sirf inputs aur outputs ko observe karta hai. Isliye ye kisi bhi model par kaam karta hai, chahe woh black-box hi kyun na ho. Ye iski sabse badi strength hai.
Q18 LIME ki limitations kya hain?
LIME brittle hai (chhoti change se explanation badal sakti hai), slow hai (bahut saare model queries chahiye), kabhi-kabhi background ko influential bata deta hai, aur kabhi-kabhi nonsensical explanations deta hai. Popular hone ka matlab reliable hona nahi hai.
Q19 Superpixels kya hain?
Superpixels image ke visually similar regions hote hain — quickshift algorithm se banaye jate hain (kernel_size=4, max_dist=200, ratio=0.2). LIME in superpixels ko perturb karta hai taaki ye samajh sake ki kaunsa region prediction ko influence karta hai.
Q20 Guided Backpropagation kya hai?
Guided Backprop DeConvNets par based hai — ye sirf positive signals ko backpropagate karta hai, aur sirf tab jab forward pass me bhi input positive tha. Result bahut sharper, zyada detailed saliency maps hote hain. Lekin ye sanity checks fail karta hai — model ke weights randomize karne par bhi map zyada nahi badalta.
Q21 Guided Grad-CAM kya hai?
Guided Grad-CAM = Grad-CAM × Guided Backprop (element-wise product). Grad-CAM batata hai "kahan" (coarse localization), Guided Backprop batata hai "kya detail" (fine-grained map). Dono ko multiply karne se high-resolution, class-discriminative map milta hai.
Q22 Adebayo et al. sanity checks kya hain?
2020 ka paper "Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps" ne dikhaya ki Guided Backprop aur Guided Grad-CAM model parameters aur training data ko randomize karne par bhi zyada nahi badalte — matlab ye maps model se zyada input image ki structure ko reflect karte hain. Agar model ke weights random hain aur phir bhi wahi map aa raha hai, to woh map model ke baare me kuch nahi bata raha. Ye explainability ki sabse badi warning hai.
Q23 Local, cohort aur global explanation me kya farak hai?
Local = ek prediction ke liye. Global = poore model ke overall behaviour ke liye. Cohort = predictions ke ek subset ke liye (local aur global ke beech). Cohort comparison Fairness testing ki buniyaad hai. Global explanation model ke behaviour ki boundaries batane wale rules nahi hain — deploy ke baad local explanations global se contradict bhi kar sakti hain.
Q24 Counterfactual explanation kya hai?
Counterfactual ek aisi scenario hai jo ulti, plausible wajah batati hai ki X kyun nahi hua. Isme proponents (jo prediction ko support karte hain) aur opponents (jo uske against jate hain) hote hain. Humans ko counterfactual explanations aksar pure attribution se zyada satisfying lagti hain, kyunki ye batati hain ki "kya badalne se nateeja badlega".
Q25 Explainability causality prove karti hai?
Nahi. Data-focused explanations se causality establish karna bahut mushkil hai, aur koi bhi explainability technique aisi nahi hai jo practically useful ho aur causality ki high guarantee de. Attribution batata hai ki kya influence karta hai, lekin ye guarantee nahi deta ki wahi wajah hai. Causality ke liye interpretable, causal models ka field dekho.
Q26 Surrogate model kya hai?
Surrogate model original complex model ka simplified version hota hai (linear, decision tree, ya rule-based) jo zyada explainable ho. Ise model distillation bhi kehte hain. Tradeoff: surrogate ka performance hamesha original se worse hota hai, aur ye guarantee nahi de sakta ki saari predictions accurately explain ho rahi hain.
Q27 Saliency map kya hai?
Saliency map image ke woh regions ya pixels highlight karta hai jo baaki se zyada important hain — jahan model apna dhyaan lagata hai. Ye gradient-based techniques se banta hai. Lekin saliency map sirf "kahan" batata hai, "kyun" nahi — isliye ise hamesha doosri techniques ke saath cross-check karo.
Q28 Sahi explainability technique kaise chunein?
Pehle 3 sawaal poochho: (1) Kaun receive kar raha hai explanation? (2) Kya explain karna hai? (3) Explanation ke baad kya hoga? Phir modality, scope aur action ke hisaab se technique chuno. Technique ko sirf isliye mat chuno kyunki try karne par explanation "achhi lagti hai" — multiple techniques se cross-check karo aur limitations document karo.
Q29 Concept Activation Vectors (CAVs) kya hain?
CAVs ek advanced technique hai jo batati hai ki model ne koi human-understandable concept (jaise "stripes" ya "red colour") kitna seekha hai, aur woh concept prediction ko kaise influence karta hai. Ye activation methods ka practical roop hai (Chapter 6). Abhi adoption kam hai kyunki har concept ke liye alag dataset chahiye, lekin ye future ka direction hai.
Q30 Explainability ka future kya hai?
Future me interactive, two-way explanations aayengi — jahan tum model se follow-up sawaal poochh sako. CAVs aur activation methods zyada practical hongi, fairness ke saath integration badhega, aur regulation (EU AI Act jaise) explainability ko legal requirement bana dega.

Honest out-of-scope list

  • Chapters 3–8 ki poori detail: Ye Early Release PDF (74 pages) sirf Chapters 1 aur 2 contain karta hai. Chapters 3–8 is PDF me nahi hain — Part III me sirf unke overviews diye gaye hain, jo book ke andar ke cross-references se banaye gaye hain. Final published book me ye chapters poore milenge.
  • Book ka GitHub repo: Book kehti hai "the GitHub repo will be made active later on" — Early Release ke time par repo active nahi tha, aur web search se bhi koi official repo nahi mila. Isliye code book me printed complete code se liya gaya hai (programmatically extract kiya, retype nahi), repo link ke bina.
  • Interviews: Is book me koi interviews nahi hain, isliye koi interview sections nahi hain.
  • Fairness: Book khud kehti hai ki Fairness ki techniques aur unhe apply karne ka tareeka kaafi alag hai — isliye ye book Fairness cover nahi karti. Cohort explanation section me Fairness testing ka reference diya gaya hai, lekin detail nahi.
  • Causality: Book saaf kehti hai ki data-focused explanations se causality establish karna bahut mushkil hai, aur koi bhi explainability technique causality ki high guarantee nahi deti. Isliye causal models is SPA me cover nahi hain.
  • Code indentation: PDF extraction me code ki indentation kho gayi thi (lines flush-left aa gayi). Code book me jaisa printed hai, waisa hi reproduce kiya gaya hai — indentation ke bina, ek note ke saath.
